title: MSK-KP Tissue Champions
bodyHtml:
MSK-KP Tissue Champions

The MSK-KP Tissue Champions Initiative is focused on efforts for aggregating single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq) maps to better understand how gene expression across cell types or disease states affects tissue function. We have assembled a team of experts across seven musculoskeletal tissue types to assist in the following efforts:

  • Creating a specification that can enable efficient data integration across the varied musculoskeletal tissues. The specification will contain areas for defining the experimental conditions needed to generate a map as well the data processing requirements needed to assess the overall quality of a map.
  • Acquiring new datasets for MSK-KP, increasing the breadth of content covered by the resource.
  • Curating tissue-specific gene programs and cell states and communicating this knowledge back to tissue-specific communities.

The list of champions and their backgrounds is summarized below. We are always looking for more contributors, so if you are interested, do not hesitate to reach out to us at help@kp4cd.org.

 

Sze Kwong "Byron" Chan, Ph.D.

Bone

Dr. Chan is an academic health researcher and postdoctoral Research Fellow in Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School. His research focuses on the signaling pathways and gene regulatory networks that control how skeletal progenitors respond to bone anabolic therapies.

 

Learn more.

Carla Cohen, Ph.D.

Muscle

Dr. Cohen is a computational biologist interested in the cells of the musculoskeletal system. Her work is part of the Human Cell Atlas project, a global consortium which aims to map all cells in the healthy human body. Currently she is analysing transcriptomic data from musculoskeletal tissues including tendon, muscle, bone and capsule to create an ethnically diverse atlas of healthy cells in adult knee and hip. This work will produce an open-source comprehensive resource for researchers around the world and will provide a foundation for further studies on human disease.

 

Learn more.

Hironori Hojo, Ph.D.

Cartilage

Dr. Hojo is a Professor at the University of Osaka whose research focuses on the molecular and gene-regulatory mechanisms that govern skeletal development, particularly cartilage and bone formation. His work investigates how transcription factors, signaling pathways, and epigenomic regulation control the differentiation and function of chondrocytes, the cells responsible for producing and maintaining cartilage.

 

Learn more.

Anne Nichols, Ph.D.

Tendon

Dr. Nichols is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Orthopaedics and the Center for Musculoskeletal Research at the University of Rochester Medical Center. Her research specializes in the molecular and cellular biology of tendon adaptation, homeostasis, injury, and tendinopathy, with a particular interest in understanding how different tendon cell populations communicate and respond to mechanical stress and injury.

 

Learn more.

Noriaki Ono, Ph.D.

Bone Marrow

Dr. Ono’s research focuses on the fundamental biology of skeletal stem cells, with a further scope on understanding pathophysiology of dental, craniofacial and skeletal deformities and diseases that affect millions of children and adults. His research has been supported by the National Institutes of Health since 2012.

 

Learn more.

Dmitriy Sheyn, Ph.D.

Intervertebral Disc (IVD)

Dr. Sheyn is an Associate Professor in the Department of Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine and a Research Scientist in the Regenerative Medicine Institute at Cedars-Sinai. His research focuses on regenerating musculoskeletal tissues—particularly intervertebral disc (IVD), bone, tendon, and other soft tissues—using adult and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs).

 

Learn more.

Sarah Snelling, MBiochem, DPhil

Tendon

Dr. Snelling is a Professor of Musculoskeletal Science at the University of Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Orthopaedics, Rheumatology and Musculoskeletal Sciences (NDORMS), where she leads the Soft Tissue Repair Group. Her research focuses on understanding the cellular and molecular biology of musculoskeletal tissues, with particular expertise in tendon and ligament health, disease, and repair.

 

Learn more.

Kevin Wei, M.D., Ph.D.

Synovium

Dr. Wei is an Assistant Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and a rheumatologist at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Dr. Wei’s research focuses on identifying novel cellular and molecular therapeutic targets in inflammatory diseases using single-cell technologies.

 

Learn more.

Marc Wein, M.D., Ph.D.

Bone

Dr. Wein is an Associate Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and an Associate Member of the Broad Institute. Marc received his B.S. and M.S. from Yale University, M.D. and Ph.D. from Harvard Medical School, and was trained in Internal Medicine and Endocrinology at Massachusetts General Hospital where he currently runs his research laboratory and clinical practice. He has received research funding and awards from the NIH, Department of Defense, American Society of Clinical Investigation, Harrington Discovery Institute, Stepping Strong Center for Trauma Innovation, American Society of Bone and Mineral Research, Endocrine Society, and the Smith Family Foundation.
